tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded browser session navigates to an admin order view for a source order (order_id=204), clicks the 'Reorder' button, which opens the Create New Order page prefilled with the source order's customer and items. The session then clicks the top 'Submit Order' button and the site navigates to a newly created Order View (observed new order id 145000008). Two deterministic element hashes were recorded and used successfully in the session: 'a1385d267e' (Reorder button) and '365c52be11' (top Submit Order button).

Task Definition:
- Build a reusable, deterministic tool that, given an admin base URL and a source order_id, reproduces the exact steps to create a new order from that existing order using the admin Reorder flow.

Action Plan:
1) Navigate to the admin order view URL for the provided order_id.
2) Click the Reorder button using the recorded elementHash 'a1385d267e'.
3) Wait a short, configurable period for the Create Order page and JavaScript to initialize.
4) Optionally extract/verify the Create Order page loaded.
5) Click the top 'Submit Order' button using the recorded elementHash '365c52be11'.
6) Wait for navigation to complete.
7) If verification requested, extract the resulting Order View page and return the new order id.

Variable Identification (inputs required):
- admin_base_url (string): the site base used to build the navigation URL.
- order_id (string): the numeric id to view the source order.
- wait_seconds_before_submit (number, optional): time to wait before clicking Submit Order to avoid 'execution context destroyed' race condition (session observed this issue).
- verify_creation (bool, optional): whether to extract the final Order View to capture the created order id.

Step Optimization and Determinism:
- Use direct URL navigation to the admin order view (no UI search) because the URL pattern is stable: {admin_base_url}/index.php/admin/sales_order/view/order_id/{order_id}/.
- Use deterministic click actions using the recorded elementHash values rather than fragile CSS selectors or text matching.
- Add explicit waits before clicking Submit Order to avoid the 'execution context destroyed' race condition observed in earlier attempts.
- Minimize steps: only actions required to reproduce the Reorder -> Submit Order flow are included. No extra filtering, sorting, or optional exploratory steps are present.

Notes about selectors and reliability:
- The two elementHash values used in the recorded session are: 'a1385d267e' for Reorder and '365c52be11' for the top Submit Order button. These elementHashes were recorded interacting with exactly one element each in the session and should be referenced to target the same controls.
- Because the admin UI requires JavaScript to initialize interactive controls, the tool includes explicit wait steps before extraction and before submission to increase reliability.

Assumptions / Constraints:
- The agent is already authenticated as an admin in the browser session; this tool does not perform login.
- The admin theme and element hashes remain stable between recordings and replays. If hashes change, selectors must be updated.
name: magento_reorder_from_existing_order
description: Create a new Magento admin order by reordering from an existing order view. Deterministic steps: navigate to the source order view URL, click the Reorder button (recorded elementHash), wait for the Create Order page to load, then click the top Submit Order button (recorded elementHash). Finally extract the resulting Order View to capture the new order id.

steps.description: Navigate to the admin Order View page for the provided source order_id.
Click the 'Reorder' button on the Order View page (recorded elementHash 'a1385d267e'). This opens the Create New Order page.
Wait for the Create New Order page to load and JavaScript to initialize. If you provide wait_seconds_before_submit, increase this wait externally before running the tool to match your environment.
Extract high-level info from the Create Order page (page title, total items present) so the run can be validated before submit.
steps.goal: Confirm the Create New Order page loaded and capture a summary of items/customer (for debug).

steps.description: Additional short wait to reduce race conditions before clicking Submit Order.
Click the top 'Submit Order' button to create the new order (recorded elementHash '365c52be11').
Wait for the Order View page navigation to complete after submitting the order.
Extract the newly created order id and basic summary (order number, date, status).
steps.goal: Capture the resulting Order View page and extract the new order id and status.

input_schema.name: admin_base_url
input_schema.description: Base admin URL of the Magento instance (example: 'http://dockerized-magento.local'). Do NOT include trailing slash.

input_schema.name: order_id
input_schema.description: Source order id numeric portion used in the admin order view URL (example: '204'). This will be placed into: /index.php/admin/sales_order/view/order_id/{order_id}/

input_schema.name: wait_seconds_before_submit
input_schema.description: Seconds to wait on the Create Order page before clicking 'Submit Order' to allow JavaScript to initialize. Default behavior uses a 3 second wait when not provided.

input_schema.name: verify_creation
input_schema.description: If true, the tool will extract the resulting Order View page after submission and return the captured new order id. Defaults to true if omitted.
